title: Reading: Installing Postgres and a SQL client

objectives.text: Identify the parts of a PostgreSQL setup: the database server, a database inside it, and a client such as psql that connects to it
Connect to a local database with psql and confirm the server version with SELECT version();
Use the psql meta-commands \l, \dt, \d and \q to list databases, list tables, describe a table and quit

unverifiedItems: Sources fetched live on 2026-10-14 (HTTP 200, receipt in sourcesRef) and the page's claims checked against the sections listed there by the author; the per-topic SME critic and its recheck (critic-sme.json and critic-sme-recheck.json in this topic's evidence) reviewed this topic against those sources and closed with no open findings; they did not re-run the platform-specific or runtime steps, so the items below remain unverified.

The simulated psql session copies output formats from a real PostgreSQL 18.3 server and psql 18.3 (captured 2026-10-13, authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/relational-design/simulator-transcripts.md); its banner and version string use the PostgreSQL 18 tutorial's example (18.6), and the socket path /var/run/postgresql is a Debian/Ubuntu packaging default that varies by platform.

The install routes' installer and package details are not stated on the postgresql.org pages in sourcesRef and are listed as unverified: Postgres.app's Initialize button, /etc/paths.d command-line path, first-connection permission prompt and default no-password user named after the macOS account; the Windows installer's postgres superuser password prompt, C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin location and auto-starting Windows service; the Ubuntu package starting the server after install and its peer authentication without -h. The client and server checks and error texts were confirmed against a real PostgreSQL 18.3 server and psql/pg_isready 18.3 on macOS on 2026-10-14; the routes themselves were not run on fresh macOS, Windows or Linux machines.
